## Exercise 1: Calculate Average Temperature

Calculate the mean of the `Temp` column in the `airquality` dataset.

```{webr-r}
# Write your code here:

```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
### 💡 Click to view Solution

```r
mean(airquality$Temp, na.rm = TRUE)
# Output: 77.88235
```
:::

## 2. Managing Workspace (`ls`, `rm`, `rm(list=ls())`)

### Exercise 2.1

```{webr-r}
b <- 20

# 2. Write your code to list all objects:

```

### 💡 Click to view Solution


:::

### Exercise 2.2
Remove only variable `a` from your environment using `rm()`.

```{webr-r}
a <- 10
b <- 20

# Remove variable 'a':

```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
### 💡 Click to view Solution

```r

# Verify with ls()

```
:::

### Exercise 2.3
Clear all objects from your working environment using `rm(list = ls())`.

```{webr-r}

```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
### 💡 Click to view Solution

```r

```

## 6. Data Manipulation (`subset`, `transform`, `within`)

### Exercise 6.1
Filter the `airquality` dataset using `subset()` to extract rows where `Temp > 90` and only keep columns `Ozone` and `Temp`.

```{webr-r}
# Write your subset() expression:

```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
### 💡 Click to view Solution

```r
subset(airquality, Temp > 90, select = c(Ozone, Temp))
```
:::

### Exercise 6.2
Use `transform()` on `df` to add a new column `Age_Months` which equals `Age * 12`.

```{webr-r}
df <- data.frame(Name = c("John", "Sara"), Age = c(21, 22))

# Write your transform() code here:

```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
### 💡 Click to view Solution

```r
transform(df, Age_Months = Age * 12)
```
:::

### Exercise 6.3
Use `within()` to modify `df` by adding an `Adult` column set to `TRUE` if `Age >= 18`.

```{webr-r}
df <- data.frame(Name = c("John", "Sara"), Age = c(21, 22))

# Write your within() expression here:

```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
### 💡 Click to view Solution

```r
df <- within(df, {
  Adult <- Age >= 18
})
df
```
:::

## 7. Missing Values (`NA`)

### Exercise 7.1
Given the vector `vals <- c(10, NA, 30, NA, 50)`:
1. Find which values are missing using `is.na()`.
2. Calculate the mean of `vals` excluding missing values.

```{webr-r}
vals <- c(10, NA, 30, NA, 50)

# 1. Identify missing values:

# 2. Calculate mean ignoring NAs:

```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
### 💡 Click to view Solution

```r
# 1. Check for missing values
is.na(vals)

# 2. Calculate mean ignoring NA values
mean(vals, na.rm = TRUE)
```
:::
